rounds.proof_sketch: Grid launched with dim3 grid(batch_size, channels, output_height*output_width). With batch_size=16 (fixed), blockIdx.x ranges [0,15]. Original condition: n >= batch_size → n >= 16, never true. Mutated condition: n > batch_size → n > 16, also never true. Both conditions evaluate identically (false) for all reachable thread indices.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the early-exit guard from 'n >= batch_size' to 'n > batch_size'. This guard is designed to catch out-of-bounds threads when the grid might be over-provisioned. However, the host code sets grid.x = batch_size exactly, meaning blockIdx.x will only range from 0 to batch_size-1 (i.e., 0 to 15). The critical boundary case where n == batch_size is never reached because CUDA guarantees blockIdx.x < gridDim.x. Since n can never equal or exceed batch_size, neither the original condition (n >= 16) nor the mutated condition (n > 16) will ever evaluate to true. The mutation is semantically equivalent under this fixed launch configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The predicate boundary (n == batch_size) is architecturally unreachable because CUDA guarantees blockIdx.x < gridDim.x, and gridDim.x is set exactly to batch_size. No value-level input change can make blockIdx.x equal batch_size.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing tools should recognize that boundary guards on block/thread indices are often unreachable when grid dimensions are derived directly from tensor dimensions. A static analysis pass could detect that (blockIdx.x >= gridDim_at_x) is always false and mark such mutations as equivalent.
